activities.name: Manta rays at Hanifaru Bay
activities.note: a protected bay in Baa Atoll, snorkel-only with daily visitor limits; outside the season mantas are still around Baa, but large feeding gatherings in the bay are rare

windows.reason: the peak, when southwest monsoon currents pack the bay with plankton and the mantas feed in numbers
the season runs May to November on the same currents

activities.name: Atoll diving
activities.note: the monsoon does not stop the diving: the southwest monsoon (roughly May to November) brings the plankton that draws mantas and whale sharks, at the cost of some visibility

windows.reason: the northeast monsoon and the Maldivian high season — calmer water and the best visibility

activities.name: Surfing the Malé atolls
activities.note: the breaks closest to the airport, such as Chickens, Cokes and Pasta Point, sit in North Malé Atoll

windows.reason: southwest monsoon swells bring the most consistent waves of the year
the shoulders of the March-to-October surf season

activities.name: Whale sharks in South Ari Atoll
activities.note: one of the few places where whale sharks are resident all year, around Dhigurah and Maamigili, though no encounter is guaranteed

activities.name: Tiger shark diving at Fuvahmulah
activities.note: the tiger sharks gather at Tiger Harbour year-round, drawn by waste from the fish market

activities.name: Bioluminescence at Vaadhoo
activities.note: the glowing plankton can appear in any month, but outside June to October it is rarely at its brightest

windows.reason: the months when the glow is most often seen, brightest on dark new-moon nights
